core_obligations: Consider the map of \'etale local rings \mathcal{O}_{Y, f(\overline{x})} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}} and record that it is flat by the cited flat-at-a-point lemma (proof lines 1086-1090).

Conclude via going down (cited Algebra lemma) that \mathcal{O}_{Y, f(\overline{x})} has a unique minimal prime when \mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}} does, i.e. Y is geometrically unibranch at f(x) (proof lines 1090-1094).
proof_roadmap: Pass to \'etale local rings and flatness of the induced map.
Transfer the unique-minimal-prime property by going down.
difficulty_reason: The proof identifies the map of \'etale local rings \mathcal{O}_{Y, f(\overline{x})} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}}, notes it is flat by the cited flat-at-a-point lemma, and uses going down for flat ring maps (cited) to transfer the unique minimal prime from \mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}} to \mathcal{O}_{Y, f(\overline{x})}, which is exactly geometric unibranchedness at the image point. The transport through \'etale local rings is the substance.
